subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this six-event AI-safety taxonomy and a permanent third-party plugin emission contract in core?
rationale: The taxonomy, permission model, public SDK shape, trust semantics, and operator interpretation become long-lived security-sensitive product contracts; code review cannot choose those contracts without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a host-owned seam
options.body: Approve the taxonomy direction only after the API is redesigned around host-bound identity, manifest policy, full validation, documentation, and installed-plugin proof.

options.title: Pause the taxonomy series
options.body: Keep the existing generic diagnostics and plugin capabilities unchanged until a narrower operator need and ownership model are agreed.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a host-owned seam
recommendation.body: Approve the taxonomy direction only after the API is redesigned around host-bound identity, manifest policy, full validation, documentation, and installed-plugin proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest ownership signal across plugin API boundaries, registry design, and the browser runtime affected by this proposal.
